name: Single-cell processing inside semi-permeable capsules on assayathon_demo
rationale: Objective is simplest_to_make, so cell culture, dissociation, quench, centrifuge washes, straining, counting and resuspension in core solution stay at the bench, where the lab has the incubator, centrifuge and pipette. Five chips follow: (1) oil-phase encapsulation, kept apart from everything else; (2) emulsion breaking, photocuring, washes and aggregate filtering on the led_405nm; (3) lysis and RT in a trap; (4) split, index PCR and pool on the thermocycler; (5) shell digestion and release. Droplets are gelled on the cold plate off chip, because a 30-minute delay line would not fit a 30 x 20 mm chip. Chip 4 uses all 6 ports for its four separate index lines. Digestion goes on its own chip because chip 4 has no spare ports. The cell filter (step 7) needs a gap of about 30 um, below the process minimum of 60 um, so it is listed as missing. The smallest droplet_junction nozzle is 200 um, so droplets will be larger than the 70 um target. The magnet is not available, so the bead clean-up stays at the bench.

chips.name: Encapsulation chip
chips.purpose: Cells in core solution are pinched into shell-polymer droplets by fluorinated oil at a flow-focusing junction.
chips.why_separate: First chip: the pump-driven cell stream starts the flow. Oil must not reach any other chip, and the gelation step that follows is off chip.

modules.does: The cell/core stream arrives on the main line (centre). The shell_polymer and fluorinated_oil lines pinch it into droplets. The nozzle is the smallest the part allows (200 um), so droplets will be larger than the 70 um target.

chips.name: Emulsion break, curing, wash and capsule filter chip
chips.purpose: Breaks the emulsion, photocures the shells, washes the capsules and removes aggregates.
chips.why_separate: Oil has to be removed before the capsules move on. This chip needs the 405 nm light, and the droplets arrive after the off-chip cold gelation.

modules.does: The mesh holds the capsules. Emulsion-breaking agent (own line) flushes the oil out, then photoinitiator is flushed in and cured under 405 nm. The same water-based reagent_line carries photoinitiator and then wash buffer, with the syringe swapped between steps.
Pillar filter with 100 um gaps removes capsule aggregates as the released capsules flow on.

chips.name: Lysis, wash and reverse transcription chip
chips.purpose: Lyses the cells, washes, and runs reverse transcription inside the capsules held in one trap.
chips.why_separate: This is a new protocol section (Methods 2.3) with warm enzymatic steps. It is kept clear of the light-curing chip.

modules.does: The mesh holds the capsules while lysis buffer, wash buffer, RT mix and wash buffer are flushed through in turn. They share one water-based reagent_line, with the syringe swapped between steps. The chip sits on a heater for the incubations.

chips.name: Split, index PCR and pool chip
chips.purpose: Splits the capsules into four portions, runs index PCR on each with its own index mix, and pools them.
chips.why_separate: Thermal cycling needs the chip on the thermocycler. Four separate index lines use all 6 ports.

modules.does: Splits the capsule stream into four equal portions.
Portion 1: index PCR with its own index primer mix, cycled on the thermocycler.
Portion 2: index PCR with its own index primer mix, cycled on the thermocycler.
Portion 3: index PCR with its own index primer mix, cycled on the thermocycler.
Portion 4: index PCR with its own index primer mix, cycled on the thermocycler.
Gathers the four indexed portions back into one stream. They carry different indexes, so they can be pooled.

chips.name: Shell digestion and cDNA release chip
chips.purpose: Digests the capsule shells to release the cDNA library.
chips.why_separate: Chip 4 has no spare ports. Digestion also runs at its own temperature, off the thermocycler.

modules.does: The mesh holds the capsules while shell-digesting enzyme is flushed in. The shells dissolve and the cDNA leaves through the outlet. The mesh keeps back any undigested debris.

off_chip.why: Culture, rinse and enzyme detachment of adherent cells in a vessel, done by the source off chip.
Quench, centrifuge and wash are done at the bench, where the lab has a centrifuge. This keeps the cell preparation off the chips.
Counting and viability check are done at the bench.
Resuspending in core solution at the loading density is a pipette step before loading the syringe for chip 1.
The emulsion is collected and gelled on the cold plate off chip. A 30 min delay line would not fit a 30 x 20 mm chip.
Bead binding, ethanol washes and elution are done as a bench kit. The lab has no magnet, so a magnetic chamber cannot be used.
Library concentration and fragment size are measured on bench instruments (fluorometer, fragment analyzer).

missing_parts.need: pillar filter with about 30 um gap (0.75 x the encapsulation nozzle) for cells upstream of the junction
missing_parts.why: A 30 um gap is below the smallest gap the process makes (60 um). The 40 um source strainer is also too coarse for protecting the nozzle.
missing_parts.workaround: Strain the cells off chip with a 30-40 um cell strainer before loading chip 1.
